raw_text:
Below is a consolidated, coach‑ready 12‑week programme for your 42‑year‑old male client (desk worker) who is 8 months post L4–L5 disc herniation, now asymptomatic and cleared with the restrictions: no heavy spinal axial loading and no loaded spinal flexion. The plan integrates strength training (3 full‑body sessions/week), two cardio sessions/week, progressive core work (safe for his back), nutrition with anti‑inflammatory emphasis, sleep & recovery protocol, and a spine‑safe 1RM test in Week 12. I give phase goals, a week‑by‑week schedule with sessions, sets/reps, RPE guidance and progressions, cardio and core programming, and recovery/nutrition guidance. Use RPE as primary intensity marker; stop any exercise that causes new or radiating symptoms and consult physio.

Quick orientation
- Frequency: Strength 3×/week (Mon/Wed/Fri recommended). Cardio 2×/week on non‑lifting days (Tue/Thu). One full rest/light day.
- Phases: Phase A (Weeks 1–4) Foundation; Phase B (Weeks 5–8) Strength & Capacity (increased push intensity per your request); Phase C (Weeks 9–12) Robustness & Test (Week 12 includes 1RM test).
- Main spinal safety rules: avoid heavy barbell back squats and conventional deadlifts; prefer trap‑bar deadlifts, kettlebell/DB hinges, chest‑supported rows, seated presses, landmine presses, unilateral work, carries. No heavy loaded spinal flexion (weighted sit‑ups, heavy cable crunches, full ab wheel from standing).
- RPE targets by phase: Phase A RPE 6–7; Phase B RPE 7–8 (some sets up to 8); Phase C RPE up to 8 on main lifts. Avoid RPE 9–10 maximal singles except the controlled 1RM test in Week 12 per protocol.
- Warm‑up: 8–12 min each session — 4–6 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility (thoracic rotation, hip hinge practice) + 1–2 light warm‑up sets for main lifts.

PHASE A — Foundation & motor control (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: reclaim movement quality, core endurance and hip strength; build base conditioning; establish safe movement patterns.

Weekly layout
- Mon — Session A (Push / Hip hinge emphasis)
- Tue — Cardio 1 (steady low impact)
- Wed — Session B (Pull / Unilateral)
- Thu — Cardio 2 (low‑intensity intervals)
- Fri — Session C (Full body & conditioning)
- Sat/Sun — 1 active recovery day (walk/mobility) + 1 rest day

Session A (example)
1. Warm‑up
2. Trap‑bar deadlift or kettlebell deadlift — 3×6–8 @ RPE 6–7
3. DB or machine bench press — 3×6–8 @ RPE 6–7
4. Single‑leg RDL (DB/Kettlebell) — 3×8/leg
5. Pallof press — 3×10–12/side (or 3×12–20s holds)
6. Farmer carry — 3×30–45 m
7. Mobility cool‑down

Session B
1. Warm‑up
2. Seated cable row or chest‑supported row — 3×8–10
3. Incline DB press or landmine press — 3×8–10
4. Bulgarian split squat — 3×8–10/leg
5. Deadbug — 3×8–10/side
6. Kettlebell swing (moderate) — 3×10–15
7. Mobility

Session C
1. Warm‑up
2. Trap‑bar RDL or kettlebell sumo deadlift — 3×10 @ RPE 6
3. One‑arm DB row (supported) — 3×8–10/arm
4. Seated DB press — 3×8–10
5. Reverse lunges — 3×8–10/leg
6. Plank variations — 3×30–60s
7. Optional 10–15 min low‑intensity steady cardio

Cardio (Phase A)
- Cardio 1 (Tue): 30–40 min steady bike/elliptical/walk at RPE 3–5.
- Cardio 2 (Thu): 25–30 min low‑intensity intervals — e.g., 1 min harder (RPE 6–7) + 2 min easy × 6–8.

Core (integrated each lifting day)
- Start each week with core finisher 10–15 min using deadbug, Pallof press, front/side planks, bird‑dog, glute bridge.

Progression Weeks 1→4
- Add small weight increases (2.5–5%) or 1–2 reps per set week to week if RPE <7 and form is solid. By week 4 aim for RPE ~7–7.5 on main lifts.

PHASE B — Strength & capacity (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase strength and pushing intensity (explicitly progressed), increase carry loads, continue spinal safety and motor control.

Weekly layout (same days)
- Monday: Session A (Trap‑bar emphasis + heavier DB bench)
- Tuesday: Cardio 1 (steady longer)
- Wednesday: Session B (Pull + seated presses)
- Thursday: Cardio 2 (intervals)
- Friday: Session C (Unilateral & conditioning)
- Sat/Sun: recovery / rest

Progression focus (push intensity increased across Phase B)
- Week 5: accumulate volume at moderate intensity
  - Trap‑bar deadlift 4×5 @ RPE 7
  - DB bench 4×6–8 @ RPE 7
  - Seated DB press 3×8–10 @ RPE 7

Core (abs) plan — integrated & progressive
- Safe core focus on anti‑extension and anti‑rotation:
  - Deadbug progressions, Pallof presses, front & side planks, bird‑dog, single‑leg bridge, suitcase/farmer carries, landmine anti‑rotation chops.
- Frequency: 2–3×/week (end of sessions or separate 10–15 min block).
- Phase progression:
  - Phase A: motor control & endurance (planks 3×20–45s, deadbug 3×8–12/side, Pallof 3×10)
  - Phase B: increase holds & unilateral challenges (planks 3×45–60s, Pallof 3–4×10–12/side, single‑leg carries)
  - Phase C: robust integrated challenges (single‑leg Pallof, loaded carries heavier, plank variations, landmine chops). Avoid heavy loaded spinal flexion throughout.

Cardio plan (two sessions/week)
- Phase A: Tue steady 30–40 min; Thu low‑intensity intervals 25–30 min.
- Phase B: Tue steady 35–45 min; Thu intervals 30 min (e.g., 8×45s hard/90s easy).
- Phase C: Tue mixed tempo 40–50 min; Thu intervals 30–35 min (1 min hard/2 min easy ×6–8 or 3×6 min tempo).
- Modalities: bike, elliptical, incline walking or pool. Prefer low impact to protect lumbar spine. Rowing only if technique impeccable and intervals short.

1RM Testing (Week 12 Friday) — safety summary
- Test trap‑bar deadlift and dumbbell bench (optional seated DB press if cleared).
- Thorough warm‑up progression, small increments (2.5–5% recommended), rest 3–5 min between attempts, limit attempts to 2–3 per lift. Stop with any new low‑back pain or radicular symptoms. Have a coach spot/observe.
- Monday and Wednesday of Week 12 follow a taper (moderate loads, lower volume) to ensure freshness.

Anti‑inflammatory Nutrition component (summary)
- Calories: slight surplus (~+200–300 kcal/day) for muscle gain or maintenance if preferred. Adjust per bodyweight/composition goals.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day depending on training volume; prioritize complex carbs around workouts.
- Fats: 20–35% calories; prioritize anti‑inflammatory fats: extra virgin olive oil, avocados, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish (salmon, mackerel) 2–3×/week.
- Emphasize colorful vegetables & fruits (berries, leafy greens), whole grains, legumes, fermented foods (yogurt/kefir), turmeric/ginger/garlic, and green tea.
- Avoid/refine: refined sugars, processed foods, trans fats, excessive alcohol.
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day, omega‑3 EPA/DHA 1–2 g/day if low fish intake, vitamin D if deficient, curcumin extract (with piperine) after consulting MD.

Sleep & Recovery (summary)
- Sleep target 7–8+ hours per night; fixed bedtime/wake time.
- Pre‑sleep wind‑down 30–60 min: reduce blue light, diaphragmatic breathing, light mobility.
- Desk microbreaks: stand/walk 3–5 min every 45–60 min; thoracic mobility.
- Post‑session recovery: 20–40 g protein + carbs within 60–90 min of hard sessions, cool‑down, light mobility, gentle heat for stiffness, and foam rolling as tolerated.
- Monitoring: daily log of sleep time/quality, resting HR, readiness score, and any back symptoms. Flags to deload: elevated RHR >6–8 bpm, persistent poor sleep, persistent soreness, or any return of radicular symptoms.

Session‑to‑session adjustments & coach notes
- Increase load conservatively: 2.5–5% increments or 1–2 reps when prescribed sets are completed at target RPE with excellent form for 2 consecutive sessions.
- Use trap bar for hinge work and avoid conventional deadlifts. Prefer chest‑supported rows to heavy bent‑over rows.
- Keep heavy axial pressing out of the program (no heavy barbell overhead press). Seated DB presses, landmine and machine presses are preferred for higher pushing intensity.
- Avoid testing or programming regular maximal singles except the controlled Week 12 1RM. Use RPE and submax testing for ongoing progress.
- If any neurological symptoms recur (leg pain, numbness, tingling), stop training and refer to physio/MD.
